Subject: Aurora: inference footprint & SKU recommendation for Dedicated capacity

Elena / Rajiv —

Thanks for the workload details earlier. I ran a quick cost/throughput sweep against the profile you shared (see attached Aurora_CAPACITY_MODEL_Q2.xlsx). High-level inputs we used:
- Target steady-state QPS: 120 inference requests/sec (avg batch sizes 1.6)
- 95th pct latency target: 120ms per request
- Typical sequence length: prompt 280 tokens, response 180 tokens (total ~460)
- KV cache hit expected for ~30% of requests (same-user continuity)

Goal for this thread: converge on a recommended Dedicated SKU mix (H100 vs A100 vs L4) and a small fallback policy so procurement can finalize pricing. Initial thoughts below; please flag anything I missed.

Preliminary recommendation (tradeoff summary):
- H100: preferred where model memory and FP16/FP8 throughput matter (large-context models, low-latency single-request spikes). Use for the primary pool that serves high-priority routes (premium customers / low-latency).
- A100: cost-effective for steady throughput for medium-length contexts when memory fits. Good as the bulk of reserved capacity if you want predictable unit economics.
- L4: lowest-cost option for high-concurrency, short-context workloads and for offloading inexpensive routes (embeddings, rerankers) — not suitable if KV cache or long context is required.

I'd like engineering to weigh in on memory constraints and whether we can meet Aurora's 120ms SLO on A100 for their model without significant quantization.

Next steps: Karthik — can you validate the microbench numbers and share a recommended instance mix (+ suggested reserved units)? Marissa — I'll need your input on how much committed capacity Aurora wants to lock vs. burst.

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas — quick pass from perf benching side. I ran the model artifact Aurora provided (gpt-infer-13b-like) across three configurations on our internal perf harness:

Microbench summary (460 tokens total, batch=1.6 avg):
- H100 (80GB, FP8/AMP): p95 lat ~90ms, sustained QPS per GPU ~70, KV cache benefits are good (host memory not a bottleneck). Memory headroom for additional context and caching.
- A100 (80GB, FP16): p95 lat ~135ms, sustained QPS per GPU ~45, borderline for 120ms SLO unless we accept small batching or offload some requests to H100 pool.
- L4 (48GB equiv, INT8): p95 lat ~220ms, sustained QPS per GPU ~30 for this context length — good for low-cost batchable routes but fails latency SLO.

Observations and tradeoffs:
1) Memory and KV cache: the 460-token working set with 13B model and KV cache means A100's 80GB fills faster when multiple concurrent sessions maintain cache. H100's memory compression (and better kernel perf with FP8) gives headroom.
2) Quantization: moving to INT8 on A100 is risky for quality unless we validate with Aurora's eval prompts; FP8 on H100 is viable and keeps latency low.
3) Autoscaling & mixing: Recommend an 60/30/10 split (A100/H100/L4) if Aurora prioritizes unit cost but wants to stay within the 120ms SLO for most traffic (route-level routing to H100 for priority). If SLO strictness is higher, flip to 30/60/10 (H100/A100/L4) to favor H100.

Attachment: radix-quant-profiles.pdf has the quantization quality delta we observed on Aurora prompts.

Karthik
Principal Applied ML Engineer

Subject: Re: Aurora: inference footprint & SKU recommendation for Dedicated capacity

Team — commercial constraints from finance/procurement that Aurora called out:
- Aurora wants 12-month committed capacity with two quarterly true-ups. They prefer a blend that maximizes predictable cost and keeps committed units compact.
- Price delta: H100 list ~2.1x A100; L4 ~0.35x A100 on unit cost basis (approx).
- Aurora is comfortable with a 20% burst window into on-demand if needed, but wants a safety net for sustained QPS.

Given Karthik's perf numbers, my recommended commercial structure for the term sheet:
- Commit to majority A100 (50-60%) to hit cost targets.
- Reserve a smaller H100 tranche (25-35%) gated by SLA tiers: premium routes auto-route to H100.
- Keep a 10-15% L4 pool for light routes and embedding jobs.

I'll draft a pricing appendix with both the 60/30/10 (cost-optimal) and 30/60/10 (SLO-first) mixes so Aurora can pick. Also propose a canary migration week to validate p95 with real traffic before ramping to full commit.

Marissa
Director, Deals & Pricing

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple clarifying points from our side:
1) The 120ms SLO was for customer-facing interactive sessions; we can accept higher latency for background/async routes (embeddings, autosuggest).
2) Our internal telemetry projects 20% KV cache hit, not 30% (I attached an export earlier) — that reduces the effective working set slightly.
3) If the A100 mix risks breaching SLO occasionally, procurement will likely push for a higher H100 blend if the difference in uptime/latency can be backed by an SLA credit.

Request: can we get a short pilot plan (1 week) that 1) validates p95 on production traffic mirrored to a dedicated pool, and 2) provides a final cost delta for the two recommended mixes (cost-optimal vs SLO-first)?

Elena
